Specification: This module is a small regression-style TLA+ specification that tests the semantics of the empty set and related constructs in TLC. It models a trivial one-variable system where x is a Boolean, the initial state sets x to TRUE, and the next-state relation leaves x unchanged, while the main substantive content is the state predicate Inv containing a sequence of checks about empty-set behavior. The checks cover SUBSET {}, UNION {}, set comprehensions over {}, function construction over {}, quantification over the empty set, DOMAIN of the empty tuple, empty ranges like 1..0, sequence membership with Seq({}), function-set expressions involving {}, and equality of unions involving empty sets; failures trigger Assert(FALSE, ...) and successes use Print(..., TRUE).
IfThenElse: IF SUBSET {} # {{}} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 1 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 1 OK", TRUE)
IF UNION {} # {} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 2 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 2 OK", TRUE)
IF {y \in {} : y = y} # {} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 3 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 3 OK", TRUE)
IF [y \in {} |-> y] # << >> THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 4 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 4 OK", TRUE)
IF (\E S \in {} : TRUE) # FALSE THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 5 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 5 OK", TRUE)
IF (\A S \in {} : FALSE) # TRUE THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 6 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 6 OK", TRUE)
IF DOMAIN <<>> # {} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 7 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 7 OK", TRUE)
IF 1..0 # {} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 8 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 8 OK", TRUE)
IF <<>> \notin Seq({}) THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 9 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 9 OK", TRUE)
IF <<{}>> \in Seq ({}) THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 10 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 10 OK", TRUE)
IF \E S \in SUBSET {} : S # {} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 11 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 11 OK", TRUE)
IF [{} -> {1, 2, 3}] # {<<>>} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 12 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 12 OK", TRUE)
IF [{1, 2, 3} -> {}] # {} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 13 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 13 OK", TRUE)
IF (UNION {{1,2,3}, {}}) # (UNION {{1,2,3}}) THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 14 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 14 OK", TRUE)
IF 1..0 # {} THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 15 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 15 OK", TRUE)
IF 1..0 # 5..2 THEN Assert(FALSE, "Test 16 Failed") ELSE Print("Test 16 OK", TRUE)
